title: Style sample: proof-canvas
objective: Show what a proof-canvas film looks like: one object constructed, then transformed so the reason is visible.
audience: The Motion Lab team, reviewing what each style template looks like before using it.

message.core_message: Half-turns carry two angles of a triangle to the third, and the three fill a straight line.
key_points: States the claim the proof explains.
Adds the one construction the proof needs.
Shows it holds for any triangle.

constraints: Silent: no narration, music or effects; the picture carries it.
Built to style template proof-canvas v1; scene roles follow its scene grammar.

research.reason: Style sample for look review, not a release. On-screen facts are a few well-established figures checked by hand; the source is named on screen. The proof is the standard parallel-line argument (Euclid I.32).

creative_directions.name: proof-canvas template
creative_directions.concept: A 22-second walk through the proof-canvas template's scene grammar on a subject that fits its visual job: Why a triangle's angles add to 180 degrees.

composition.approach: Portrait only: copy in the top band, the hero in the middle, captions above the bottom UI zone.

creative_directions.pacing: A planned visual event at least every 2 seconds.
creative_directions.why_it_fits: It is the template's own grammar, so the sample shows the template rather than one film's choices.

success_criteria: Each scene role of the template is recognisable
No frame holds still for more than 2.5 s
